title: coordination-notice.v1 — one advisory cross-session coordination signal
description: The typed payload of one advisory coordination notice (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#939, eADR-0043). A notice is the durable carrier a peer worker session reads and then acts on ONLY by re-verifying canonical state — it never carries authority. Every behaviour-driving field is a closed enum; there is deliberately no free-prose slot, because a notice is ultimately read by a model. The repo-native identifier fields (branch, paths) are the one attacker-influenceable surface and are render-constrained by the writer, not by this schema. The engine assembles a notice by construction through coordination_notice.render (keyword-only required parts); this schema is the CLI-boundary gate and the drift anchor for the closed vocabularies. additionalProperties is false everywhere so an unknown field is a hard error rather than a silent carrier of unvetted content.

schema_version.description: The notice format version. A reader that does not recognise the version skips the notice (forward compatibility lives in the reader, not here).

notice_id.description: A per-notice random identifier (secrets.token_hex(16)). Excluded from the condition fingerprint, so it never affects dedupe; present so a live poke can name exactly one notice.

kind.description: The coordination purpose. A closed set — additive-only, one new value per deliberate decision, drift-test pinned. Never free text.

event.description: The specific event within the kind. Constrained per-kind by the allOf branches below, so an event that does not belong to its kind is a hard error.

emitter.description: Who emitted the notice, in repo-native terms only. Never a session identifier, worktree path, or machine name (eADR-0043 law 5) — those never reach a durable surface.

audience.description: The work item this notice is POSTED ON — the surface the receiving session reads. At least one of pr/issue.

subject.description: The canonical object the receiver must RE-VERIFY (never trust from the notice). paths are the attacker-influenceable field — capped at 20 and render-constrained by the writer.

verify.description: How the receiver re-establishes truth. action names the canonical read to run; observed pins what the emitter saw, for comparison — never a substitute for the read.

action.description: The canonical re-verification the receiver performs. Each maps to one real read (queue status, base ancestry, durable plan block, overlap recompute, PR state) or none.

observed.description: The emitter's observed evidence pins, all optional. Compared against a fresh read; the action→required-field coupling is enforced in render code and drift-tested, not here.

emitted_at.description: When the emitter composed the notice, ISO-8601 UTC (e.g. 2026-08-18T14:03:11Z). Measurement data; the platform's own comment timestamp is the trusted time. Excluded from the fingerprint.

branch.description: A git branch name in the conservative render-safe charset (letters, digits, dot, underscore, slash, hyphen). The writer render-constrains before this gate; the pattern is the belt.

work_ref.description: A repository-native reference to a unit of work: at least one of pr/issue/branch. No session identity.
